title: The Code at the Door
intro: A text says a courier is outside with your parcel. This time you can talk back.
Pick your replies and sniff each message as it arrives.
Every chat ends with your choice. Choose wisely.

notify.text: I am outside with your parcel. Please send me the code…

msg.text: Hi! I am outside with your parcel.
send me the code that just arrived on your phone

msg: so I can hand it over.

replies.text: I did not order anything. Who sent you?

sys.text: Orrin Bank: 482913 is your login code. Never share it with anyone.

msg.text: Quickly please, I have 20 more parcels today.

replies.text: That text is from my bank. Why do you need it?

msg: It is a gift, from someone who likes you 😉

msg.text: The code is how I confirm it is you.

replies.text: Fine, I will read you the code
I will check with the courier's own app

msg.text: It is just the delivery code, the bank name is a coincidence.

replies.text: A bank code is never a delivery code. I will tell my bank.

outside.label: Out-of-the-blue visit
outside.lens: You did not order anything, and the "driver" is texting from a number you do not know.
outside.why: A surprise delivery with a request for a code is a way to start a conversation.

code.label: Asks for a code
code.lens: It asks you to send the code that just arrived on your phone.
code.why: No delivery needs a code from your phone. Anyone who asks for it is a scammer.

bankcode.label: The code is from your bank
bankcode.lens: The code in the text says "login code". It is your bank's, not the courier's.
bankcode.why: Someone is trying to log in to your bank right now. They need you to read them the code.

rush.label: Hurry
rush.why: Rushing you is a pressure trick.

gift.label: "Someone likes you"
gift.lens: A parcel from a mystery admirer.
gift.why: A gift story is a hook, not a reason to hand over a code.

delivery.label: "Just a delivery code"
delivery.why: Explaining away the bank name does not change what the code unlocks.

actions.label: Check with the courier's own app and tell my bank

block_report.line: Blocked and reported. Your bank also saw the login attempt fail, since you never sent the code.

verify.line: The courier's app showed no parcel for you. Your bank blocked the login attempt. Case cracked.

go_ahead.line: The code let Mirage log in to your bank and move money out within minutes.

what_if.go_ahead: The text with the code said "login code" and "never share". Reading that line once was the way out.
what_if.verify: Checking was smart. Blocking and reporting as well helps others.

golden_rule: A login code is for you alone. If someone asks you to read it out, it is a scammer, whatever the story.

quick_check.q: A "driver" asks you to send the code that just arrived by text from your bank. What do you do?

options.text: Send it, they have a parcel for you
Send it, but only after they confirm your name
Never share it. Block and report, and tell your bank

quick_check.explain: That code lets someone log in as you. Nobody real ever needs it, not even part of it.

hints.nudge: Look at the text with the code. Whose code is it?

rows.v: Is only for you to log in
